findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.violation: Three sentences in one paragraph name what appears to be the same underlying item under three different terms in a row (stipend item, reimbursable item, covered purchase amount) with no signal that they refer to the same thing, so the reader cannot tell whether one item or three different items are being described.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the item, for example stipend item, and use it in all three sentences instead of switching to reimbursable item and covered purchase amount.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing. The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request.
findings.violation: Paragraph 2 states that the request has already reached final processing and that the employee gets a confirmation email once processing finishes, then paragraph 3, opened with Then to signal a following step, has the employee review a confirmation summary and submit the final request only after that. A reader working through the section in the order written cannot tell whether the request was already processed or still needs to be submitted.
findings.fix: Reorder the steps so the employee reviews the confirmation summary and submits the final request before the manager signs it and finance confirms the budget line, matching the order the reader actually performs them in.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.violation: Of the paragraph's four sentences, only the first is about the section's own topic, stipend request coordination. The remaining three move through an unrelated travel expense audit, evolving federal remote work guidance, and the office coffee budget, with nothing connecting any of them to program coordination or to each other, so a reader finishing the section cannot state what it was actually about.
findings.fix: Remove the audit, federal guidance, and coffee budget sentences, or move each to its own relevant section, and keep this section limited to stipend request coordination.

findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the employee directly as you in the first and third sentences, then the middle sentence, Countersign the employee request within two business days, is an instruction an employee cannot carry out on their own request; it reads as an instruction for the manager, but nothing marks the shift, so the reader cannot tell which reader the middle sentence is for.
findings.fix: State who countersigns explicitly, for example The manager countersigns the employee's request within two business days, so the instruction is not mistaken for something the employee does.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.violation: The series' 2 items mix grammatical forms (gerund, other) at their head words instead of sharing one form.
findings.fix: Restate every item in the series with the same grammatical form.

findings.evidence: The finance liaison publishes the vendor list on the first business day of the month.
findings.violation: The sentence's newest elements, the finance liaison and the vendor list, both appearing for the first time in the document, are stated mid-sentence, then the sentence ends on the first business day of the month, a timing detail the reader already has from the identical publishing cadence given earlier for the equipment catalog and the reimbursement log, so the end position is occupied by repeated information rather than the new content.
findings.fix: Reorder the sentence so it ends on the new information, for example On the first business day of the month, the finance liaison publishes the vendor list.
